title: Filament response heuristics — scratchbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick brain dump for an experimental lightweight response orchestration idea — "filaments" as tiny response fragments assembled progressively. Goal is to reduce tokens spent on the expensive model while preserving perceived quality for common short-answer flows (help, short facts, one-step actions).

Core concept (working):
- A request can be answered by a chain of micro-responses (filaments). Each filament is a concise semantic unit (1–3 sentences / 8–40 tokens) produced by a cheaper model or cached snippet and optionally stitched, expanded, or validated by a higher-fidelity model later.
- Filament types: factual, clarification, actionable-step, template-graft, persona-tag. We classify early by heuristic signals (prompt length, user intent classifier, confidence from the cheap model).
- Runtime: first-line cheap-filament to meet latency SLO; if user continues or a quality gate fails, escalate to refine or replace with a high-fidelity pass.

Why this might matter (hypotheses):
- Cut average per-request hosted-token cost by >=25% for short-turn workloads (support chat, FAQ style threads).
- Keep p95 latency low (cheap first byte) while allowing heavy-duty model only for escalation.
- Improve tail reliability via cached filaments + quick fallback.

User stories (rough):
- As a customer support end user, I get a quick probable answer instantly; if it's insufficient I see a refined answer shortly after without re-sending my question.
- As a developer, I can opt-in per-route filaments with simple config: cheap-model, high-fidelity-model, expansion-window (ms), confidence-threshold.

Acceptance signals / success metrics:
- Cost: average token-cost / short-turn drops by 20–30% on targeted routes in a 2-week experimental cohort.
- UX: user click-to-satisfaction (in-widget thumbs-up) not degraded by >5% vs baseline.
- Latency: median first-byte latency improves by 30% for targeted routes; p95 not worse than baseline more than 2% of the time.
- Quality: automated eval suites for 500 prompt seeds — cheap-first + escalate chain passes quality gates >=90% of baseline.

Design / implementation sketches:
- Router decides filament path using lightweight intent classifier (local candidate, threshold 0.7). If cheap model returns high-confidence answer (internal score > C1), serve immediately with tag: "filament:cheap:confident" and async fire-and-forget high-fidelity verification.
- If cheap model returns low-confidence or user accepts escalate, spin up a scoped higher-fidelity request that can either replace prior output or append a correction recap.
- Cache keys: hash(intent-signature + route-config + top-k tokens) -> filament snippet. Cache TTLs short (minutes) but aggressive for high-frequency queries.

Instrumentation to add:
- token_cost_by_filament (cheap, expansion, verify)
- first_byte_ms_by_route + p95_response_time_split(cheap-only, escalated)
- filament_cache_hit_rate and mean_cached_response_age
- mismatch_rate (cheap_answer vs verify_answer diff > threshold)

Risk and unknowns:
- Brand safety & hallucination: cheap model hallucinations could be served quickly and persist via cache -> need conservative gating and ephemeral caching for low-confidence classes.
- User confusion: multiple answers (quick then refined) could appear as contradictory. Small UX affordances needed ("refined answer" label, change log).
- Complexity: adds routing logic, additional telemetry and cost accounting; needs clear opt-in per route.

Experiment plan (MVP):
1) Canary routes: docs/search API and support-short-answer route (10% traffic).
2) Cheap model: gpt-small-quant or tuned 6B, high-fidelity: default-prod-large.
3) Simple gating: if cheap_confidence >=0.8 -> serve + async verify; if 0.5<=conf<0.8 -> serve with ephemeral cache + sync verify (blocking up to 600ms), if conf <0.5 -> direct high-fidelity.
4) Collect metrics for 2 weeks, compare cost and UX signals.

Mock config example (route-level):
- route: /support/quick
  cheap_model: rwd-small-6b-q
  verify_model: rwd-latest-34b
  confidence_thresholds: {fast:0.8, sync:0.5}
  expansion_window_ms: 800
  cache_ttl_seconds: 300

Notes / open questions to discuss with SRE & Trust:
- Where to run cheap model? Edge vs hosted cheap pool? Tradeoffs re: colocated inference vs one more network hop.
- Data retention for filament cache (PII risk) — must honor redwood redaction config.
- How to label/visualize answer transitions in client SDKs (socket events, websocket deltas, server-sent events).

Next actions (near term):
- Sync with Maya (product) & Ishaan (serving-runtime) to validate feasibility and rough cost calc.
- Prototype a minimal router + cache in dev environment, target one route. 1-week spike.
- Draft an experiment doc with measurement plan and rollout guardrails (conservative default: off for enterprise default).

Random brainlets / heuristics ideas (scratch):
- "micro-certainty" token: cheap model emits a single-token confidence tag that router uses; useful for tiny fast decisions.
- serve templated filaments for common ask types (definition, steps), then pipeline expands variables with a verify pass.
- allow client to request "only-fast" mode or "always-accurate" via header for power users.

Unsaved TODOs:
- pull example transcripts from support and estimate expected cache hit uplift (Maya)
- list safe categories that can be cheap-first (non-PII, definitions, static product info)
- sketch SDK surface for incremental updates (JS + iOS)

-- end of scratchbook --
(keep as a messy personal note; we'll prune into an experiment PRD if team wants to run this)
